name: Camp Lemonnier
status: Largest US overseas base in Africa. 4,000+ personnel. Drone operations, special forces staging, counterterrorism hub.

name: NSA Bahrain / US 5th Fleet HQ
status: Headquarters of US Naval Forces Central Command and US 5th Fleet. ~8,000 personnel. Controls Gulf naval operations.

name: Al Udeid Air Base
status: Largest US air base in the Middle East. Houses CENTCOM forward HQ and Combined Air Operations Center. 10,000+ personnel.

name: Camp Arifjan
status: Primary US Army staging base in the Gulf. Logistics hub for Iraq/Afghanistan operations. ~13,000 personnel at peak.

name: Naval Station Yokosuka
status: Homeport of US 7th Fleet and carrier strike group. Largest US naval facility in the western Pacific. ~27,000 personnel.

name: Kadena Air Base
status: Largest US Air Force base in the Pacific. Hosts F-15s, KC-135 tankers, surveillance aircraft. Keystone of Indo-Pacific air power.

name: Camp Humphreys
status: Largest US overseas military base by area. USFK headquarters. ~28,500 personnel. Deterrence against North Korea.

name: Naval Base Guam / Andersen AFB
status: Strategic bomber base and submarine port. B-52 and B-2 rotational deployments. Key node in second island chain defense.

name: Ramstein Air Base
status: HQ US Air Forces in Europe and NATO Allied Air Command. Critical airlift and C2 node. ~9,000 US personnel.

name: Aviano Air Base
status: US 31st Fighter Wing. F-16 operations covering Mediterranean and Middle East. Supported operations in Libya, Iraq, Syria.

name: NAS Sigonella
status: Hub for Mediterranean maritime patrol, drone operations, and logistics. Known as the 'Hub of the Med.' Supports Africa operations.

name: Naval Station Rota
status: Homeport for 4 Aegis BMD destroyers. Gateway to Mediterranean and Atlantic. Ballistic missile defense for NATO Europe.

name: RAF Lakenheath
status: Largest US Air Force base in UK. F-15E and F-35A wings. First US F-35s deployed in Europe. ~4,500 military personnel.

name: Incirlik Air Base
status: Joint US-Turkish base. Reportedly stores ~50 US B61 nuclear gravity bombs. Key staging for Middle East operations.

name: Pituffik Space Base (Thule)
status: Northernmost US base. Ballistic missile early warning radar and satellite tracking. Critical for Arctic and space domain awareness.

name: Pine Gap
status: Joint US-Australian signals intelligence facility. Satellite surveillance, missile tracking, and intelligence collection. One of the most important SIGINT sites globally.

name: Naval Support Activity Souda Bay
status: Deep-water port supporting US and NATO naval operations in the eastern Mediterranean. Ammunition storage and logistics hub.

name: Diego Garcia
status: Remote atoll hosting bomber runway, naval port, and intelligence facilities. Strategic mid-Indian Ocean power projection platform.

name: Al Dhafra Air Base
status: Hosts ~3,500 US personnel. F-35, F-22, U-2, RQ-4 operations. Premier US ISR and 5th-gen fighter base in the Gulf region.

name: Muwaffaq Salti Air Base
status: US drone and fighter operations against ISIS. F-16s and MQ-9 Reapers. Key staging for Syria/Iraq strikes. ~3,000 US personnel.

name: Naval Station Norfolk
status: World's largest naval station. Homeport of US 2nd Fleet and NATO's Allied Command Transformation. 75+ ships, 134 aircraft.

name: Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam
status: HQ US Indo-Pacific Command. Pacific Fleet homeport. Strategic hub for all US military operations across the Indo-Pacific theater.

name: Naval Station Guantanamo Bay
status: Oldest US overseas naval base (1903 lease). Strategic position at Windward Passage between Cuba and Haiti. Detention facility and logistics.

name: Camp Bondsteel
status: Largest US base in the Balkans. Built 1999 for KFOR mission. ~7,000 capacity. Maintains stability in Southeast Europe.

name: Lask Air Base
status: Rotational US fighter deployments since 2012. F-22 and F-35 rotations. Part of enhanced NATO eastern flank posture.

name: Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base
status: Expanding US rotational base near the Black Sea. MQ-9 drones and troop deployments. Adjacent to NATO Aegis Ashore BMD site at Deveselu.

name: Keflavik Air Base
status: P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol operations resumed 2016. GIUK gap monitoring. Critical for tracking Russian submarine activity in the North Atlantic.

name: THAAD Battery Guam
status: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense system protecting Guam from ballistic missile threats. Part of integrated Pacific missile defense architecture.

name: Fort Iwakuni (MCAS Iwakuni)
status: US Marine Corps air station. F-35B Lightning II squadron. First forward-deployed F-35Bs in the Pacific. ~5,000 Marines.

name: Camp Butler (Okinawa)
status: III Marine Expeditionary Force HQ. ~18,000 Marines across Okinawa installations. Rapid response force for western Pacific contingencies.

name: PLA Support Base Djibouti
status: China's first overseas military base, opened 2017. ~2,000 personnel capacity. Pier accommodates large warships. 2km from Camp Lemonnier.

name: Ream Naval Base
status: Chinese-funded expansion since 2022. Can berth PLA Navy vessels. Gives China a foothold in the Gulf of Thailand.

name: Gwadar Port Facilities
status: China-built deep-water port under CPEC/BRI. Dual-use infrastructure with rumored military facilities. Overlooks Strait of Hormuz approaches.

name: Tajikistan Outpost (GBAO)
status: Confirmed PLA outpost in Gorno-Badakhshan since ~2019. Small garrison near Afghan border. First known PLA ground facility in Central Asia.

name: Solomon Islands (Security Pact)
status: Security pact signed 2022 allows Chinese naval port calls and police deployment. No permanent base yet. Pacific island chain contestation.

name: Fiery Cross Reef
status: Artificial island with 3km runway, hangars, radar, CIWS, anti-ship missiles. Largest PLA installation in the Spratlys. Operational since 2016.

name: Subi Reef
status: Artificial island with 3km runway, radar arrays, SAM emplacements, and barracks. Part of China's 'Big Three' militarized reefs.

name: Mischief Reef
status: Artificial island with runway, anti-ship cruise missiles, SAMs. Within Philippines EEZ. Rejected by 2016 Hague ruling. Fully militarized.

name: Woody Island (Yongxing)
status: PLA's South China Sea administrative and military HQ. J-11 fighters, HQ-9 SAMs, YJ-62 anti-ship missiles. Runway, port, and radar.

name: Hambantota Port
status: 99-year lease obtained 2017 via debt-equity swap. Strategic dual-use port on Indian Ocean shipping lanes. India's primary 'String of Pearls' concern.

name: Doraleh Multipurpose Port
status: China Merchants-built commercial port adjacent to PLA base. Dual-use logistics node. Part of integrated Djibouti military-commercial complex.

name: Equatorial Guinea (Bata Port — planned)
status: Reported negotiations for PLA Navy's first Atlantic Ocean base. Would transform China's global naval reach. Under US pressure to reject deal.

name: Chittagong (BRI Port Access)
status: China-funded deep-water terminal. Dual-use container and potential naval logistics node. Part of BRI Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar corridor.

name: Myanmar (Kyaukpyu Port)
status: China-built deep-water port on Bay of Bengal. Direct pipeline/road to Kunming bypasses Malacca Strait. Strategic BRI bypass route.

name: Tartus Naval Base
status: Russia's only Mediterranean naval base. Expanded 2017 on 49-year lease. Services submarines and warships. Future uncertain after Assad's fall in 2024.

name: Hmeimim Air Base
status: Main Russian air base in Syria since 2015 intervention. Su-35, Su-34 operations. Air defense umbrella over eastern Mediterranean. Status uncertain post-Assad.

name: Sevastopol Naval Base
status: HQ of Russia's Black Sea Fleet since 18th century. Annexed with Crimea 2014. Severely degraded by Ukrainian strikes since 2022.

name: Kaliningrad Military District
status: Heavily militarized exclave between NATO members Poland and Lithuania. Iskander missiles, Baltic Fleet HQ, S-400 air defense. NATO's biggest A2/AD concern.

name: 102nd Military Base Gyumri
status: ~5,000 Russian troops. MiG-29s and S-300. Russia's foothold in the South Caucasus. Lease extended to 2044. Relevance questioned after 2020/2023 Azerbaijani offensives.

name: Port Sudan Naval Base (planned)
status: Agreement signed 2020 for 300-person logistics hub. Would give Russia Red Sea naval access. Delayed by Sudan civil war but not cancelled.

name: Cam Ranh Bay Access
status: Former Soviet naval base. Russia retains periodic port access for warships and submarines. Reduced from Cold War peak but still used.

name: Vladivostok (Pacific Fleet HQ)
status: HQ of Russia's Pacific Fleet. Submarine base, surface fleet, and naval aviation. Counterbalance to US Pacific presence. Nuclear submarine pens at nearby Rybachiy.

name: Murmansk / Severomorsk (Northern Fleet HQ)
status: HQ of Russia's most powerful fleet. Ballistic missile submarines, carrier Admiral Kuznetsov. Arctic operations and nuclear second-strike capability.

name: Novorossiysk Naval Base
status: Secondary Black Sea Fleet base. Relocated assets from Sevastopol after Ukrainian strikes. Growing importance as primary operational Black Sea port.

name: 201st Military Base Dushanbe
status: Russia's largest overseas ground force base. ~7,000 troops. Guards Afghan border and projects power across Central Asia. Lease to 2042.

name: Kant Air Base
status: CSTO collective rapid reaction force air component. Su-25 attack aircraft. Only Russian air base in Central Asia.

name: 999th Air Base (Belarus)
status: Russian air defense and tactical nuclear weapons deployed to Belarus since 2023. S-400 systems. Forward nuclear positioning against NATO.

name: Africa Corps — Mali (Bamako/Timbuktu)
status: Formerly Wagner Group, rebranded Africa Corps under GRU. ~1,500 personnel. Replaced French forces. Combat operations against insurgents. Mining access deals.

name: Africa Corps — Burkina Faso
status: Russia Africa Corps deployed after 2022 coup. Training junta forces, counterinsurgency. Gold mining concessions in exchange for security.

name: Africa Corps — Central African Republic
status: Wagner/Africa Corps present since 2018. Guards presidential compound, runs diamond/gold mines. Documented human rights abuses. ~1,000 personnel.

name: Africa Corps — Libya (East)
status: Wagner/Africa Corps supports Haftar's LNA. Based near Al Jufra and Brak al-Shati air bases. MiG-29s and Su-24s deployed. ~1,200 fighters.

name: Africa Corps — Niger
status: Deployed after 2023 coup that expelled French and US forces. Training junta military. Replaced US drone base at Agadez. Uranium access.

name: Nagurskoye Air Base (Arctic)
status: Northernmost military base in the world. Renovated 'Arctic Trefoil' complex. MiG-31 interceptors. Guards Northern Sea Route and Arctic resources.

name: RAF Akrotiri
status: British Sovereign Base Area. Staging point for Middle East operations. Used in strikes on ISIS and Yemen/Houthi targets. SIGINT facilities.

name: Dhekelia Garrison
status: British Sovereign Base Area on eastern Cyprus. Signals intelligence station at Ayios Nikolaos. Army garrison and logistics support.

name: Gibraltar Naval Base
status: Controls western Mediterranean chokepoint. Nuclear submarine berths. Forward logistics for Royal Navy Atlantic and Mediterranean operations.

name: HMS Juffair / UK NSF Bahrain
status: UK Naval Support Facility reopened 2018. Base for Royal Navy's Gulf operations and Combined Maritime Forces. First permanent UK base east of Suez since 1971.

name: Mount Pleasant Complex
status: Built after 1982 war. RAF Typhoon fighters, Rapier air defense, army garrison. Ensures UK sovereignty over Falklands and South Atlantic.

name: HMNB Clyde (Faslane)
status: Home of UK's Trident nuclear submarine fleet. All four Vanguard-class SSBNs based here. Britain's continuous at-sea nuclear deterrent.

name: British Forces Brunei
status: Gurkha battalion and jungle warfare training school. UK's only permanent military presence in Southeast Asia. ~2,000 personnel.

name: BFC Duqm (Oman)
status: Joint logistics base at Port of Duqm. Supports Royal Navy carrier strike group Indian Ocean deployments. Opened 2019. Alternative to Gulf bases.

name: Forces Francaises a Djibouti
status: France's largest overseas base. ~1,500 troops. Pre-positioned armor, Mirage 2000 fighters. Key to operations in Sahel and Horn of Africa.

name: French Forces UAE (Naval Air Station)
status: French naval and air base near Abu Dhabi, opened 2009. Rafale fighters, naval berths. ~650 personnel. France's Gulf presence.

name: Base Navale de La Reunion
status: French Indian Ocean naval base. Patrols southern Indian Ocean EEZ. Supports operations from Mozambique Channel to Kerguelen Islands.

name: French Forces New Caledonia
status: French Pacific garrison. ~1,500 troops. Maintains sovereignty and projects force across South Pacific. Key amid China's Pacific expansion.

name: Elements Francais au Senegal
status: Long-standing French military presence in Dakar. Reducing from ~350 to minimal presence as part of post-colonial drawdown across West Africa.

name: Base Aerienne Adji Kossei
status: France's Sahel air operations hub. Mirage 2000 and drone base. Withdrawal announced 2024-25 as France exits Sahel post-coup wave.

name: French Forces Cote d'Ivoire
status: ~900 French troops at Port-Bouet. Largest remaining French base in West Africa. Logistics and training hub. Drawdown planned by 2025.

name: French Forces Gabon
status: ~350 French troops at Camp de Gaulle, Libreville. Pre-positioned equipment for Central Africa operations. Drawdown announced 2024.

name: FAZSOI (Mayotte)
status: French naval detachment in Mozambique Channel. Patrols critical shipping lane between Madagascar and East Africa. Foreign Legion presence.

name: French Forces French Polynesia
status: French military garrison covering vast Pacific EEZ. Maritime surveillance and sovereignty patrols. Former nuclear test infrastructure at Moruroa.

name: Turkish Base Al-Tariq
status: Opened during 2017 Qatar blockade. ~5,000 Turkish troops. Armor and special forces. Turkey's first Gulf military base.

name: Camp TURKSOM
status: Turkey's largest overseas military base. Trains Somali National Army. ~200 Turkish military trainers. Opened 2017 in Mogadishu.

name: Al-Watiya Air Base
status: Seized by Turkish-backed GNA forces 2020. Turkish air defense systems and drone operations. Extends Turkish power across central Mediterranean.

name: Turkish Forces Northern Cyprus
status: ~30,000 Turkish troops stationed since 1974 invasion. Largest overseas Turkish garrison. Controls northern third of Cyprus island.

name: Turkish Observation Posts (Idlib)
status: Network of ~15 observation posts and bases across Idlib and northern Aleppo. Protects Turkish-backed opposition zone. ~10,000+ troops across northern Syria.

name: Turkish Base Al-Bab / Afrin
status: Turkish military presence across Euphrates Shield and Olive Branch operation zones. Controls ~4,000 sq km of northern Syria. Military and proxy forces.

name: Suakin Island Base (planned)
status: 2017 agreement to rebuild Ottoman-era port and establish naval facility. Delayed by Sudan instability. Would give Turkey Red Sea access near Bab el-Mandeb.

name: Turkish Base (Azerbaijan/Nakhchivan)
status: Joint Turkish-Azerbaijani military facility. Enhanced after 2020 Karabakh war. Turkish F-16s deployed during conflict. Monitors Iran's northern border.

name: INS Dweeprakshak (Agalega)
status: India-built airstrip and jetty on Agalega island, operational 2024. Extends Indian maritime surveillance deep into the Indian Ocean.

name: Andaman & Nicobar Command
status: India's only tri-service theater command. Controls Malacca Strait western approaches. Naval, air, and army assets. Strategic chokepoint watch.

name: Assumption Island Facility (planned)
status: Planned Indian naval facility. Agreement signed but implementation delayed by Seychelles domestic politics. Would extend Indian Ocean surveillance arc.

name: Farkhor Air Base
status: India's first overseas air base. Renovated Soviet-era facility. Provides strategic depth against Pakistan and monitors Afghanistan. Operated since 2002.

name: Duqm Port Access
status: Access agreement for Indian Navy at Port of Duqm. Dry dock for Indian warships. Covers western Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden approaches.

name: Changi Naval Base Access
status: Bilateral logistics agreement. Indian Navy vessels regularly dock for resupply. Joint exercises. Eastern Indian Ocean chokepoint cooperation.

name: INS Kadamba (Karwar)
status: India's largest naval base (Project Seabird). Nuclear submarine pen, aircraft carrier berth. Covers Arabian Sea and western Indian Ocean. Expanding to 2x current size.

name: Israeli Intelligence Presence
status: Reported Israeli intelligence and drone staging cooperation. Proximity to Iran's northern border. Facilitated intelligence collection and potential strike planning.

name: Israeli Presence Somaliland
status: Emerging Israeli security footprint following post-Dec 2025 recognition. Intelligence cooperation, potential naval access on Gulf of Aden.

name: Ramon / Nevatim Air Bases
status: Israel's primary F-35I Adir strike bases. Long-range strike capability covering Iran, Red Sea, and eastern Mediterranean. Underground hardened facilities.

name: Haifa Naval Base
status: Israeli Navy HQ and submarine fleet base. Dolphin-class submarines with reported nuclear second-strike capability. Eastern Mediterranean dominance.

name: NATO Aegis Ashore Deveselu
status: US-operated NATO ballistic missile defense site. Aegis Ashore system with SM-3 interceptors. Russia considers this a primary security threat.

name: NATO Aegis Ashore Redzikowo
status: Operational 2024. SM-3 interceptors. Completes European BMD shield with Deveselu. Triggered Russian warnings of targeting with nuclear weapons.

name: NATO JFC Brunssum
status: NATO Joint Force Command responsible for northern Europe. Commands NATO's Very High Readiness Joint Task Force. Upgraded since 2014 Russia reset.

name: NATO JFC Naples
status: NATO Joint Force Command responsible for southern Europe, Mediterranean, and Africa. Commands NATO's southern flank operations including maritime.

name: Tapa Military Base (NATO eFP)
status: UK-led NATO Enhanced Forward Presence battlegroup. ~1,200 troops from multiple NATO nations. Deterrence on Russia's Baltic border.

name: Adazi Military Base (NATO eFP)
status: Canada-led NATO eFP battlegroup. Scaling up to brigade-size. Multinational force deterring Russian aggression on NATO's eastern flank.

name: Orzysz Military Base (NATO eFP)
status: US-led NATO eFP battlegroup near Suwalki Gap. Critical corridor between Kaliningrad and Belarus. Most vulnerable point on NATO's eastern flank.

name: Steadfast Defender Forward HQ (NATO)
status: New NATO forward command element at Magdeburg, activated 2024. Coordinates eastern flank defense. Part of NATO's largest restructuring since Cold War.

name: Aksaz Naval Base
status: NATO Standing Naval Group Mediterranean home port. Turkish Navy base supporting Alliance Mediterranean operations and chokepoint control.
